newsitem.title: UK: Shell sees delay in release of Nigerian detainees.
newsitem.headline: Shell sees delay in release of Nigerian detainees.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell RD AS said on Thursday the release of the remaining workers held by Nigerian villagers since the weekend at the Egwa Two flow station on the Niger Delta would be delayed.
"The boat which was going to pick up the remaining 52 from Egwa was delayed this morning and left Warri this afternoon," a Shell spokesman said.
He was unable to give any indication of when the detainees would be finally freed.

Delicate negotiations between Shell and Ijaw tribesmen, who seized six flow stations in the western Niger Delta on Saturday as part of a local government dispute, have secured the release of most of the 127 Shell workers held captive.

The occupations, together with the shutdown of five more flow stations in the eastern Delta region have forced Shell to reduce production by about 210,000 barrels per day (bpd) and warn of disruption to April exports.
